solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Giving up work soldier finds arduous

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, standing for a soldier
an arduous task is tiring

explanation.surface: A soldier finds the hard slog of his job wearing and decides to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring is the act of leaving employment for good, so it describes giving up work.

clue.text: Turn down in the matter of colour

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning or with regard to
buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone declines a proposal concerning the choice of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff is to reject or refuse bluntly, a synonym of turning something down.

definitions.meaning: plants give off water vapour through their leaves, breathing it out

explanation.surface: Something seems to occur just by breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to come to pass and, in botany, to give off vapour through pores.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the heavens come below the scripture

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the school subject of scripture
the heavens are the sky

explanation.surface: An exclamation that propping up holy writ is a hazardous business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation but is the noun meaning the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky and dangerous are synonyms: both describe something involving a chance of harm.

clue.text: Like an innocent criminal alive in New York

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the two letters for the city
criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An innocent person is ensnared by a live criminal in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns ALIVE into AIVEL, which goes 'in' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent person is guileless, and acting naively means behaving with that simple trust.

clue.text: Lay with fool returning from Ukrainian port

parts.note: a lay is a poem or song, as is an ode

indicators.note: returning means the word for the fool is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A balladeer comes back from a Black Sea port with an idiot in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Odesa, often spelt with two S's, is a major Black Sea seaport in Ukraine.

indicators.note: contains signals that one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: diction is a speaker's manner of delivery
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A parcel delivery turns out to hold a vinyl record and a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction is a representation of something, the same thing as a picture of it.

definitions.meaning: ... as in remains or lodges somewhere
a corset, laced to slim the waist

explanation.surface: Someone settles on a garment to look thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means remains in place, and the plural noun names an old-fashioned laced corset worn to shape the figure.

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is viewed as supporting the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun for an old saying; 'revolutionary' rearranges HIM AS PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, which is exactly what an aphorism is.

parts.note: bears means holds up or supports
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A valuable financial holding underpins the family's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means of the head: the tall fur cap worn by guardsmen is a head's asset.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is a tall fur hat, so it is an asset for the head, capital punningly meaning of the head.

clue.text: Display prominently that parking is included in rent

indicators.note: included in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a rent is a tear or slash
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A landlord advertises loudly that a parking space comes with the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid but is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash a story is to give it prominent display, as in a newspaper headline.

indicators.note: keeps signals that one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Destiny holds a son who is out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea figuratively means bewildered, which is being lost.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a shy person is self-conscious

explanation.surface: A dubious character becomes embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy is an informal word for questionable or arousing suspicion.

clue.text: Cutter's carrying gold so one gets rid of spirits

indicators.note: carrying signals one word holding the other inside it

parts.note: an exciser is one who cuts out; the 's is 'is'
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A surgeon is bearing gold, so someone banishes ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorciser drives out evil spirits or demons from a person or place.

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A strong aircraft climbs to an unknown altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty and powerful are synonyms, both meaning possessing great strength.

clue.text: Manic fits, yet Chris's in treatment

indicators.note: treatment suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite his wild outbursts, Chris is undergoing therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in treatment' rearranges YET CHRIS'S, its final S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics are uncontrollable outbursts of emotion, exactly a bout of manic fits.

clue.text: Stumbles outside church? One stretches out an arm!

indicators.note: outside signals one word wrapped around the other

parts.note: trips means stumbles
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone trips in front of a church and flings out an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps muscle extends the forearm, straightening the arm at the elbow.

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
a tour is a journey
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Employees gauge how long a trip takes.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants, a retinue or staff accompanying someone important.

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a stop is a block or hindrance
a page is a young servant; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An obstacle puts an end to a domestic worker's walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a work stoppage, a cessation of work as a form of industrial strike.

clue.text: Acts of betrayal aren't so bad

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone argues that disloyal deeds are not so terrible after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, a word that can cover such acts collectively.

parts.note: n.o. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for not out
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A batter remains in and is busy at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter still in at the end is 'not out', printed n.o. on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Here 'this time' points to a time of day, and midday is such a time.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means precise or detailed

explanation.surface: A precise moment.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means precise or very detailed; as a noun it is a sixty-second span.

indicators.note: consuming signals one word swallowing the other

parts.note: to mate is to couple
in means fashionable or popular
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A pair takes a fashionable drug before the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film, a type of show.

definitions.meaning: the greatest warrior of Troy in the Iliad

explanation.surface: A Trojan who pushes others around.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of the Trojan prince in Homer, and as a verb it means to bully or browbeat.

clue.text: Had final stroke in game and died

definitions.meaning: in croquet, hitting the ball against the final peg to finish
a slang phrase for passing away

explanation.surface: A player made the last shot of the match and then expired.
explanation.definitionFit: In croquet one finishes by striking the peg, and the phrasal verb is slang for having died.

clue.text: Georgia adopts one brought up in Italy

indicators.note: adopts signals one word taking the other in

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the word one taken as written

explanation.surface: A family in Georgia takes in a child raised in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ONE into ENO, which GA 'adopts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a port city in northern Italy, so it is a place found in that country.

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
use is custom or practice

explanation.surface: Rodents have been found in a GP's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' suggests a surgery but means custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a small rodent regarded as a pest, so one of the vermin.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath

parts.note: more means extra or additional

explanation.surface: A society backs extra traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the essential customs and conventions of a community.

parts.note: to loose is to untie

explanation.surface: A family member of easy morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a relative, and this is the familiar form of that word.

indicators.note: tortuously means in a twisting way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unexpected bend was taken along a winding route.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undreamt of was never imagined, so it was not foreseen.

clue.text: Pass by the Spanish church's feature

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article
an apse is a semicircular recess in a church

explanation.surface: A tourist walks past a Spanish church's architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or slips by.

parts.note: men means people
to swear is to promise solemnly

explanation.surface: Folk vow to wear clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is clothing for men, a category of garments.
